about: S3.4 citation checker, spec test T07 — the TUNING set. Fictional documents only. Expectations are what a careful lawyer checking the citations by hand would conclude, written before the check was run on them. G5–G7 were the first held-out set; they became tuning data once they informed a change. G8–G10 were the second held-out set. G11–G13 were the third held-out set (Phase 3 gate, run once on citations-s3.4e); a lettered sub-paragraph it showed (CPR r. 3.4(2)(a)) was fixed in citations-s3.4f, so it became tuning data.

citing.title: Brief extract

BRIEF EXTRACT (fictional)

1. The claim arises under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 and 28 U.S.C. § 1331.
2. The standard is set out in Palmer v. Oakridge Freight, 544 F.3d 210 (7th Cir. 2008), and Lindqvist v. Harrow Corp., 87 F. Supp. 3d 455 (S.D.N.Y. 2015).
3. A contrary view appears in Morrow v. Pell Industries, 310 F.4th 88 (12th Cir. 2022) and Quist v. Delane, 45 F.6th 12 (9th Cir. 2019).
4. In England, see [2017] UKSC 59, [2008] UKHL 48 and [2016] UKHL 7; and Hadley v Baxendale (1854) 9 Exch 341.
5. In the EU, see Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Directive 2011/83/EU and Case C-311/18.
6. Employers must also follow 29 C.F.R. § 1910.1200.

SHARE PURCHASE AGREEMENT (fictional)

6. Warranties
6.1 The Seller warrants to the Buyer that each Warranty is true and accurate at the date of this Agreement.
6.2 The Warranties are qualified by matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
6.3 No claim may be brought for breach of Warranty unless notified within eighteen (18) months after Completion.

7. Limitations
7.1 The Seller's aggregate liability for all Claims shall not exceed the Purchase Price.
7.2 The Seller is not liable for a Claim of less than GBP 25,000 (fictional).

Schedule 4 Warranties
1. The Company has filed all tax returns when due.

citing.title: Disclosure memo
citing.text:
DISCLOSURE MEMORANDUM (fictional)

1. Background
1.1 This memo concerns the Share Purchase Agreement (the "SPA").

2. Time limits
2.1 Under section 6.3 of the Share Purchase Agreement, claims must be notified "within eighteen (18) months after Completion".
2.2 By clause 7.2 of the SPA, the Seller is not liable for small claims.

3. Warranties
3.1 Clause 6.2 of the Share Purchase Agreement qualifies the Warranties by "matters disclosed in the Disclosure Letter".
3.2 The tax warranty is paragraph 1 of Schedule 4 of the Share Purchase Agreement; the property warranties are in Schedule 5 of the Share Purchase Agreement.
3.3 Clause 7.1 of the Share Purchase Agreement caps liability at "the Purchase Price" and clause 7.4 of the Share Purchase Agreement excludes consequential loss.

sources.title: Facility Agreement
sources.text:
FACILITY AGREEMENT (fictional)

19. Representations
19.1 Each Obligor makes the representations and warranties set out in this Clause 19 to each Finance Party.
19.4 No Default is continuing or might reasonably be expected to result from the making of any Utilisation.

22. Financial Covenants
22.1 The Borrower shall ensure that Leverage in respect of any Relevant Period shall not exceed 3.50:1.
22.2 The Borrower shall ensure that Interest Cover in respect of any Relevant Period shall not be less than 4.00:1.

27. Events of Default
27.1 An Obligor does not pay on the due date any amount payable pursuant to a Finance Document unless payment is made within three Business Days of its due date.

Schedule 3 Conditions Precedent
1. A copy of the constitutional documents of each Obligor.
2. A copy of a resolution of the board of directors of each Obligor.

citing.title: Advice letter on the facility
citing.text:
ADVICE LETTER (fictional)

1. Covenants
1.1 Under Clause 22.1 of the Facility Agreement, the Borrower must ensure that ‘Leverage in respect of any Relevant Period shall not exceed 3.75:1’.
1.2 Interest cover is tested under Clause 22.2 of the Facility Agreement, which requires that Interest Cover ‘shall not be less than 4.00:1’.
1.3 There is no equity cure: Clause 22.5 of the Facility Agreement is silent on the point.

2. Default
2.1 Non-payment is an Event of Default under Clause 27.1 of the Facility Agreement, subject to a grace period: payment must be made ‘within three Business Days of its due date’.
2.2 The board resolution required by paragraph 2 of Schedule 3 of the Facility Agreement has been delivered.

3. Law
3.1 The duty to promote the success of the company is in section 172 of the Companies Act 2006, and limitation runs under section 5 of the Limitation Act 1980.
3.2 See also [2023] EWHC 101 (KB) and [1998] EWCA Civ 12.

expect.text: within three Business Days of its due date

citing.title: Litigation memo
citing.text:
LITIGATION MEMO (fictional)

1. Jurisdiction
1.1 Removal is governed by 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a) and Fed. R. Civ. P. 81(c).

2. Standard
2.1 See Tolland v. Brixham Mills, 571 U.S. 402 (2014); Okafor v. Lakeshore Bank, 140 S. Ct. 1201 (2020); and Vance v. Mercer Logistics, 812 F. App'x 330 (3d Cir. 2020).
2.2 California courts agree: Ruiz v. Halberd Corp., 61 Cal. Rptr. 3d 97 (Cal. Ct. App. 2007). But see Dunmore v. Stack, 288 So. 4th 15 (Fla. 2019) and Pryce v. Allard, 77 F.3d 501 (5th Cir. 2029).

3. Europe
3.1 Jurisdiction within the EU follows Regulation (EU) No 1215/2012; whistleblowers are protected by Directive (EU) 2019/1937.

4. Summary
4.1 As paragraph 2.1 above explains, the standard is settled. Paragraph 5.2 sets out next steps.

citing.title: Skeleton argument
citing.text:
SKELETON ARGUMENT FOR THE CLAIMANT (fictional)

1. The contract
1.1 Under clause 15.3 of the Supply Contract, either party may terminate on notice.
1.2 Clause 9.1 of the Supply Contract says that "The Supplier shall not be liable for any indirect loss."
1.3 The Defendant also relies on clause 21.4 of the Supply Contract, which does not help it.

2. Procedure
2.1 The application is made under CPR r. 3.4(2)(a) and, in the alternative, CPR Part 24.
2.2 The Defendant cites CPR Part 112, which does not exist.

3. Authorities
3.1 See [2021] EWCA Civ 1405 and [2015] UKSC 36; and Hadley v Baxendale (1854) 9 Exch 341.
3.2 The Defendant's reliance on [2007] UKSC 12 is misplaced.
